summary: [standards] `of_io` tests `raw_os_error() == Some(5)` before the error kind and the comment says 'EIO is 5 on every platform canon runs on'. canon ships x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (build-native.yml, publish.yml), where os error 5 is ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED: std maps it to ErrorKind::PermissionDenied [INFERENCE: std source, not run on Windows; CI tests run on ubuntu only, so nothing would catch it]. On Windows every refused read (and `of_text` on '(os error 5)' texts) would become the subject's `*_UNAVAILABLE` with retryable true, the inverse of the ATIP 1.3 rule these codes implement (DENIED is not retryable). One-line fix: match `e.kind()` first (PermissionDenied -> Denied) and apply the raw-5 EIO test only after, or under `#[cfg(unix)]`; the unit tests use `from_raw_os_error(13)` for denied, so they are unix-only too (say so, or build the errors from ErrorKind). Blast radius: all 14 `_UNAVAILABLE` codes and every `*_DENIED` the helpers pick.
